caption:
Apple is now selling its first paid add-on for Apple Intelligence: a $49.99 "intelligence usage pack" in Logic Pro 13.
It is a one-time top-up for Creator Studio subscribers who hit their monthly AI limit.
Packs for Siri AI, Image Playground and Photos tools are expected later.

Would you pay extra to keep using AI on your Apple devices?

site_article.headline: Apple starts selling $49.99 Apple Intelligence usage packs in Logic Pro
site_article.dek: The one-time top-up is Apple's first paid add-on for AI use, and it starts with Creator Studio subscribers.
site_article.summary: Apple has begun selling $49.99 intelligence usage packs that extend AI limits in Logic Pro 13 for Apple Creator Studio subscribers. It is the first time Apple has charged separately for Apple Intelligence usage.
site_article.seo_title: Apple Intelligence usage packs: $49.99 for extra AI in Logic Pro
site_article.seo_description: Apple now sells $49.99 one-time packs that add AI usage in Logic Pro 13 after the monthly limit. What they cover, who can buy them and what comes next.
site_article.answer_summary: Apple Intelligence usage packs are $49.99 one-time purchases that add AI usage after a Creator Studio subscriber hits the monthly limit. They start in Logic Pro 13 and do not work with Family Sharing.

paragraphs.text: Apple has started charging separately for Apple Intelligence usage. Logic Pro 13, which reached the Mac App Store on November 5, 2026, includes a Buy More Usage option that sells a single item: a $49.99 intelligence usage pack. 9to5Mac reported the option on the morning of November 9. Until now, Apple Intelligence features have been free on Apple devices.

The pack sits under Logic Pro, Intelligence Features, Show Usage. According to Apple's support document, as cited by both outlets, it is a one-time purchase rather than a subscription. Extra usage is only consumed after the regular monthly limit is reached, unused usage rolls over from month to month, and a pack expires 12 months after purchase.

The packs are tied to Apple Creator Studio, the subscription that bundles Apple's creative apps. In the United States it costs $12.99 a month or $129 a year, according to Tech Between the Lines. Subscribers get the Logic Pro assistant up to a monthly limit and pay again beyond it. People who bought Logic Pro outright for $199.99 do not get the assistant.

Packs do not support Family Sharing. Creator Studio can be shared with up to five other people, but only the Apple Account signed in to iCloud at the time of purchase can use a pack. Tech Between the Lines reported that the packs are sold in eight countries for now: Brazil, Canada, France, Germany, India, Mexico, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Apple's support document does not say how much usage $49.99 buys, and it gives no fixed monthly allowance for the Logic assistant, whose limit depends on how complex conversations are. Other Creator Studio limits are listed, including at least 50 generated images a month, according to Tech Between the Lines.
What the Logic Pro assistant does

The assistant is a chat panel inside Logic Pro that can act on a project, such as setting up a vocal track from one request or starting a new song, and it answers questions about the app. It is labeled beta, needs a Mac with Apple silicon running macOS 27 or later, and works in US English only. Tech Between the Lines noted that sources differ on which models power it, with Apple's support document naming Google Gemini.

9to5Mac expects packs to reach Final Cut Pro, Pixelmator Pro and the iWork apps when their Creator Studio updates arrive later in November. Packs for other server-based features, including Siri AI, Image Playground and Photos editing tools, are expected later, without dates. Tech Between the Lines wrote that Apple described extra access to such features in June as part of most iCloud+ plans.

The price is notable next to the subscription it sits on. At $49.99, a single pack costs nearly four months of Creator Studio, and buyers cannot see in advance how much work it covers. Cloud AI requests cost money to serve, and the packs pass part of that cost to the heaviest users instead of raising the base price for everyone.

For most iPhone owners nothing changes yet. The Logic Pro packs only affect paying Creator Studio subscribers who reach a monthly cap. The larger question is how Apple handles the same model for Siri and Image Playground, features used by far more people.
Watch whether Apple publishes how much usage a pack includes, and whether the packs for Siri AI and Image Playground arrive as one-time top-ups or inside iCloud+ plans.
